items.title: Multi-agent parliament: 5 specialized AI agents vote on each trade with consensus threshold
items.content:
5 AI agents vote before I put a single dollar on Polymarket.

If at least three disagree, the bet does not go through. In 14 days this system beat a single agent by 23% on ROI.

Here is how it works.

I used to run one agent. One model, one prompt, one context, and no adversarial validation.

It gave an answer in seconds and was right 60% of the time. But the remaining 40% ate the profit entirely, because it was wrong with the same confidence it had when it was right.

This is the classic single-agent overconfidence problem. A model does not know how to doubt if it has nobody to argue with.

So I built a system in Claude Code that I call the parliament.

It has five agents, and each one has its own specialization: geopolitics, macroeconomics, science, sports, crypto.

Before every position on Polymarket they all receive the same market, and each one analyzes it through its own lens.

Each agent is a separate system prompt with a strict scope. The geopolitics agent does not see on-chain data. The macroeconomist does not read Twitter. They work in isolated contexts, and this is fundamental: if you give them all the same information, they arrive at the same conclusion, and the whole point is lost.

Data is fed through structured input. Each agent receives the Polymarket market as JSON: name, current odds, deadline, trading volume.

On top of that, each gets its own set of sources:

> geopolitics: diplomatic briefings + sanctions lists
> macroeconomist: Fed minutes + CPI data
> crypto agent: whale alerts + sentiment score from Twitter

After the analysis comes the vote with a strict consensus threshold: minimum three out of five.

But this is not just counting hands. Each agent returns a confidence score from 0 to 100 and detailed reasoning.

If the parliament splits 3:2, the agents in the minority are required to produce a dissent report: a counterargument with specific sources. I read it before confirming the position.

Results over 14 days across 47 markets:

> single agent: +$640
> parliament: +$1,120

With fewer bets. It simply filtered out the junk at the gate.

> win rate: 60% → 74%
> average size of loss dropped by half

The system refused to enter markets where the agents could not agree among themselves.

But the most unexpected part involves the science agent, which I added last, almost as an experiment.

It ended up in the minority more often than any other and voted against on 19 out of 47 markets. When it was the only one voting against while the other four were in favor, it turned out to be right four times out of five.

Those are four positions I would have entered without it and lost a total of $890. One dissenting agent was worth more than the entire rest of the system combined.

The problem with AI trading is not the quality of the model. The problem is that everyone builds one smart agent and then acts surprised when it confidently loses money.

Five agents forced to argue with each other is not five opinions. It is a built-in mechanism of doubt that a single model does not have and never will. The parliament is not smarter than any of its members. It simply does not let any one of them be confident alone.

This whole system, honestly, was born from something much simpler. Before the parliament, before the agents, and before any automation, I was just watching smart wallets on Polymarket through a Telegram bot: https://t.co/6oJMPDWj4z

I watched who was consistently earning, broke down their trades, and tried to understand why they entered those specific markets and not the ones next to them.

The idea for the parliament came from one observation: the five most profitable wallets almost never bet on the same thing at the same time. They thought differently, and that is exactly what made each of them profitable.

items.title: Why prediction market bots fail: incomplete backtesting data

Your Polymarket bot is failing for one simple reason:

Your backtest is USELESS.

It's because your data is incomplete.

You're missing order book depth, real spreads, and most importantly actual fill behavior.

That's why your bot looks profitable on paper but breaks the moment you go live.

You're not simulating reality.

Fix is simple, but almost nobody does it.

Build a recorder and start now.

Track every tick of every market you trade, including price changes and full order book depth.

Also record every external data source you rely on like NOAA, ESPN, Binance, or Coinbase.

You need pre-window and post-window data too, because timing is where most of the edge comes from.

The biggest mistake is fills.

If your model assumes perfect execution, it's already wrong.

That's exactly why people complain about getting only 40% fills live.

You need scale.

At least 1000 windows for statistical confidence, which is around 10 days on 15m markets.

AI coding tip most people ignore:

Your model isn't getting worse, it's just drifting.

As sessions get longer, AI slowly loses structure.

Instructions blur, logic breaks, outputs become inconsistent.

That's AI drift.

Most people try to fix it with:

• MD files = good for context, bad for structure
• JSON = strict logic, but messy for long workflows

Neither solves the core problem.

Here's the trick.

Use TOML.

It sits right in the middle.

Readable like markdown, but structured like JSON.
Clear sections, clean hierarchy, no chaos.

When you force AI to operate through TOML, something changes.

It keeps track of state better.
Logic stays consistent across steps.
Less hallucination, less drift over time.

Why?

Because you're giving the model both context AND structure in one format.

That's what it actually needs to stay stable.

If you're building bots, automations, or anything long-running, this matters a lot.

Bad structure = broken outputs.
Clean structure = consistent execution.

Most people blame the model, but it's usually just how you feed it.

The $31 Billion Edge: Use the New AI Swarm GitHub to Automate Your Alpha

most traders are walking into a digital slaughterhouse because they are fighting against ai agent swarms with a manual button and a prayer. this is the new regime of the market where the big firms have already moved past simple algorithms and into the realm of digital soldiers that never sleep. i spent hundreds of thousands of dollars on developers in the past for apps thinking i would never be able to code myself. through losing money with liquidations and over trading i knew i had to automate my trading so i learned to code live on youtube for the world to see

code is the great equalizer because it allows a regular person in a bedroom with a whiteboard to compete with wall street. if you are still clicking buttons by hand you are playing a game that is already rigged against you. i used to be the guy staring at the charts at three in the morning just hoping for a bounce only to wake up to a liquidation email. why do we trade by hand when we know for a fact that when emotions hit you cannot think logically which is a fact backed by a stanford professor 

the trap that most people fall into is thinking they can hire their way to success or find a magic bot that prints a billion dollars overnight. i realized that with bots you must iterate to success which is why i decided to learn everything live. now i have fully automated systems trading for me instead of getting liquidated every time the market wicks. the core of this system is the rbi framework which stands for research and back test and implement 

most people spend their lives looking for a shortcut but the only real edge is building a list of great trading ideas and testing them constantly. if an idea worked in the past it is much more likely to work in the future. i have seen people with zero coding knowledge learn to back test their strategies within fifteen days and completely change their lives. one good trading bot can wipe out every bad financial decision you have made in your entire life because success becomes repeatable once it is automated 

the problem with most ai on the internet is that it is pure fugazi or fake promises that never actually execute in a live market. i just pushed a massive update to my open source github that adds over twenty different ai agents for trading. these are not just simple scripts but fully functional agents that can handle everything from sentiment analysis to funding arbitrage. i am putting all of this out for free because i was wrong about open source being bad and i think this code needs to be in the hands of the people

we just added support for the newest models like gpt 5 nano and gpt 5 mini and even claude 4 point 5 before they were even fully available to the public. i built a model registry that allows you to easily update these models as they drop every couple of months. this ensures that your trading system is always using the sharpest intelligence available in the world. the key is having a testing framework that can query every single one of these models with a simple prompt to verify they are working 

the real magic happens when you move beyond a single model and into the realm of the swarm. most traders think that an ai can just tell them when to buy or sell but that is a dead end. llms alone cannot trade for you but they can be used as a corrective second layer on top of a proven strategy. this is why i built the swarm agent which queries multiple models from different companies in parallel to get a unified answer 

imagine asking claude and gpt and gemini and deepseek and llama the same question at the exact same time. the swarm agent collects all of those responses and then uses a consensus reviewer to give you a final decision. this removes the bias of any single model and gives you a diverse perspective on your trading decisions. if seven models say yes and one says no you have a much higher confidence level than just blindly following one ai 

this layer of intelligence is what protects you from taking stupid trades when your strategy triggers. we are layering these agents on top of quant logic that we already trust. the agent acts as a gate or a final layer that can ratify or refuse a trade based on the current market regime. i built this because tools do not replace edges but they certainly amplify them once you find an anomaly in the market 

one of the most powerful tools we just added is the exchange manager which allows you to switch between exchanges with a single line of code. most of our trading has been on chain on solana but i wanted to implement hyperliquid support for perps and leverage. the exchange manager acts as a router that handles the differences between on chain contract addresses and exchange symbols. now you can run the same agent on solana for spot trading and hyperliquid for leverage with zero coding changes in the agent itself 

this makes the system future proof because we can add more exchanges like base chain or poly market as the opportunities arise. the goal is to be able to route different tokens to different exchanges based on liquidity and fees. i want to make switching exchanges as easy as changing a single value in your config file. this is how we stay ahead of the game and move faster than the people who are still hard coding every single function 

i also built a specific agent for housecoin which is based on the thesis that one house equals one housecoin. this agent uses the dca strategy to accumulate housecoin when the price is below the sma but only after consulting the ai swarm. i believe every real estate agent and homeowner in the world will eventually need housecoin as a hedge. real estate is a three hundred trillion dollar market and having an agent that can smart dca into that position is a massive edge 

the housecoin agent is a perfect example of a research based strategy being automated. it tracks the twenty day and five minute smas while respecting daily spending caps and trading hours. the ai decision layer analyzes fifty five bars of price data before each trade to confirm the signal. this is the type of sophisticated system that used to be reserved for the billionaires like jim simons

jim simons ran up a net worth of thirty one billion dollars by realizing there are patterns in the market that robots can trade but humans can never. he simply executed his own rbi framework for years on end and built a system of testing and deploying. my goal is to make automating your trading simple so you can do it as a regular person without a big team. jim changed bloodlines by creating generational wealth and i believe code can do the same for you if you put in the work 

the biggest risk you can ever take is to not learn how to automate your trading if you are already a trader. hand traders lose money because they are human beings built with emotions that clash with logical decision making. if you are committed to building a provable edge then you need to embrace these principles. join me in the discord and grab the code on github to start building your own swarms today 

this is a rare once in a decade opportunity to rethink how we interact with the web and the markets. ai agents are clearly the future and the entire workforce will be replaced or at least using these flows. i will keep contributing to this open source framework and placing all of my agents there for free. code is the great equalizer and i want to make sure the people have the tools to win
